title: GH#17549: fix concurrent worker deaths — DB archival + dispatch stagger
body:
## Summary

- New `opencode-db-archive.sh` script archives OpenCode sessions older than 14 days to a separate DB, reducing the active DB from 11.4 GB to ~3.3 GB
- Increases dispatch stagger from 2s to 8s (`PULSE_DISPATCH_STAGGER_SECONDS`) between worker launches to reduce concurrent write contention

## Root Cause

OpenCode's session database uses `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 0`. When the pulse dispatches 8+ workers simultaneously, they all write to the same 11.4 GB SQLite DB after every tool call. With zero retry on lock contention, any `SQLITE_BUSY` kills the session silently — `step_start` fires, 0 tokens returned, exit code 0.

- **Single worker tests pass** — no contention
- **Batch of 8 all fail** — constant lock contention
- **Both Anthropic and OpenAI models affected** — it's the DB, not the API
- **Upstream issue filed**: anomalyco/opencode#21215

## Archive Script (`opencode-db-archive.sh`)

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `archive` | Move sessions >14d to archive DB |
| `archive --dry-run` | Show what would be archived |
| `archive --retention-days 30` | Custom retention |
| `archive --max-duration-seconds 30` | Time-budget for pulse pre-flight |
| `stats` | Show row counts and age distribution for both DBs |

Current stats show **12,169 sessions** (69%) eligible for archival. The archive DB preserves all history for memory lookup and session mining.

**Pulse integration**: Call from pulse-wrapper.sh pre-flight:
```bash
opencode-db-archive.sh archive --max-duration-seconds 30
```

## Verification

- `bash -n` — syntax OK for both files
- `shellcheck --severity=warning` — zero warnings
- `opencode-db-archive.sh stats` — returns correct counts
- Stagger delay is configurable via `PULSE_DISPATCH_STAGGER_SECONDS` env var (default 8s)

## Related PRs

- #17572: TTL alignment fix (Layer 5/6 dead zone)
- #17577: Worker observability + claim guard

Closes #17549

title: GH#17584: tighten Closes keyword rule to prevent accidental issue auto-close
body:
## Summary

- Changes the traceability rule in `build.txt` from "PR body MUST include `Closes #NNN`" to "exactly ONE `Closes #NNN` for the issue the PR directly solves"
- Adds explicit guidance: context references use `Related: #NNN` or `See #NNN`, NEVER `Closes`

## Root Cause

Line 198 of `build.txt` told every agent to always include `Closes #NNN`. When a PR mentioned an issue for context (e.g., PR #17587 explaining *why* the git-pull fix was needed referenced #17584), `Closes #17584` auto-closed the simplification issue on merge — even though the PR didn't do the simplification work.

#17584 was auto-closed twice:
1. By alex-solovyev's worker (stale checkout, closed as "Invalid")
2. By PR #17587 (git-pull fix that referenced #17584 for context with `Closes`)

## What changed

```diff
- PR body MUST include `Closes #NNN` — only mechanism creating GitHub PR-issue link.
+ PR body MUST include exactly ONE `Closes #NNN` for the issue the PR **directly solves**.
+   GitHub auto-closes issues when PRs with `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #NNN` merge.
+   NEVER use `Closes` for context references — use `Related: #NNN` or `See #NNN` instead.
```

Related: #17584

title: GH#17549: nohup worker launch to survive pulse-wrapper exit
body:
## Summary

- Wraps worker launch with `nohup` so workers survive the pulse-wrapper's exit
- One-line change: `"${worker_cmd[@]}"` → `nohup "${worker_cmd[@]}"`

## Root Cause

launchd runs pulse-wrapper with `StartInterval=120` and `KeepAlive=false`. Each cycle completes its dispatch/merge work and exits. When bash exits, it sends SIGHUP to all background jobs — including workers launched via `&`. Every worker dispatched today died at the exact same moment (when the pulse-wrapper exited), not at random times.

The earlier SQLITE_BUSY analysis (DB archival + stagger) addressed a real contention issue but was not the primary kill signal. Evidence: all workers in a batch died simultaneously at pulse-wrapper exit time, not at random points from DB lock contention.

## Why nohup

- `nohup` ignores SIGHUP — the signal bash sends on exit
- `$!` still captures the worker PID (unlike subshell + disown)
- The EXIT trap only calls `release_instance_lock` (removes lock dir) — no child process killing
- macOS lacks `setsid`; `nohup` is the portable equivalent for SIGHUP immunity

## Verification

- `bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — syntax OK
- PID tracking unchanged (`$!` works with nohup)
- Stagger delay and dispatch comment still work (they run after the launch line)

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: High (polling loop / process lifecycle)
- **Plan**: Deploy, wait for next pulse cycle, verify workers survive the wrapper exit
- **Status**: `pending-verification` (will verify post-merge)

Related: #17549

title: GH#17549: fix false completion signal preventing worker retries
body:
## Summary

- Fixes `output_has_completion_signal()` to only check model text output, not file contents read by the model
- Workers that die mid-turn will now correctly trigger the continuation retry loop instead of being falsely classified as "success"

## Root Cause

Worker 72882 (issue #17574) read `full-loop.md` which contains `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` as documentation text. The completion check grepped the raw `tee` output and found the marker — classifying the run as complete even though the worker never created a PR, committed, or pushed. The continuation retry (exit 77) never fired.

Evidence: log had `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE: 1` match but zero `git commit`, zero `git push`, zero `gh pr create` — the marker was from a file read, not the model's own output.

## Fix

Parse the OpenCode JSON stream and only check:
- `"type":"text"` events (model's own text output)
- `"type":"tool_use"` `input.command` (commands the model invoked)

Ignores `"type":"tool_use"` `output` (file contents, command output). Falls back to raw grep for non-JSON output (Claude CLI).

## Verification

```
PASS: correctly detected NO completion signal (tool output ignored)
PASS: correctly detected completion signal in model text
```

title: GH#17599: fix now_ms fallback and add WAL cleanup trap in opencode-db-archive
body:
## Summary

Addresses two medium-severity findings from the Gemini review of PR #17582 on `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh`.

### Fix 1: Simplify `now_ms()` fallback chain (line 85)

**Before**: Always spawned `python3` first (even on Linux where GNU `date` supports `%3N`), then `perl`, then arithmetic fallback.

**After**: Tries `date +%s%3N` first and validates the output is a 13+ digit integer (guards against macOS `date` which outputs `%3N` literally). Falls back to `python3`/`perl`/arithmetic only when needed. On Linux this avoids spawning a Python interpreter entirely.

### Fix 2: Robust cleanup for `ATTACH DATABASE` / `DETACH DATABASE` loop (line 420)

**Before**: `ATTACH`/`DETACH` were within the same `sqlite3` heredoc invocation (so the attachment releases on process exit), but the archive WAL was not checkpointed on early return or signal delivery between batches.

**After**: Added `_checkpoint_archive_db()` top-level helper with a global idempotency flag (`_ARCHIVE_CHECKPOINT_DONE`). Registered via `trap '_checkpoint_archive_db "$ARCHIVE_DB"' RETURN` at the start of the batch loop section. Fast-path explicit call before the incremental vacuum on normal completion prevents double-run. Follows the project's established `trap '...' RETURN` cleanup pattern (see `tech-stack-helper.sh`).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh  # zero violations
```

Closes #17599

title: GH#17596: tighten completion detection in JSON parsing block
body:
## Summary

Addresses two review findings from PR #17595 on `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

### HIGH (line 1562): False-positive completion detection

The JSON-path block previously exited 0 if `model_text` contained `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge`, or `git push` — regardless of whether those commands succeeded. This could match commands the model merely mentioned in its reasoning or invoked but that failed.

**Fix**: Mirror the fallback block's logic — require both model intent in `model_text` AND a success signal in `raw`:
- `gh pr create`: requires `pull/` or `created pull request` in raw
- `gh pr merge`: requires `merged` in raw (case-insensitive)
- `git push`: requires `-> ` or `branch ` in raw

### MEDIUM (line 1548): Single-pass field extraction

The extraction for `text` events only checked `part.text`. The extraction for `tool_use` events only checked `part.state.input.command`. OpenCode JSON events can have fields at multiple levels.

**Fix**: Check multiple common paths in a single pass:
- Text: `obj.text` → `part.text` (with short-circuit)
- Tool input: `obj.input` → `part.input` → `state.input` (with short-circuit)

## Verification

The fallback block (non-JSON path) is unchanged and continues to work as before. The JSON-path block now has equivalent strictness to the fallback block for command-success checks.

Closes #17596

title: GH#17549: add canary smoke test and two-phase activity watchdog
body:
## Summary

- Adds a canary smoke test that gates worker dispatch — runs a trivial `opencode run` with 20s timeout to verify the runtime is functional before committing to a full task
- Replaces the single-phase activity watchdog (300s) with a two-phase design: fast kill (30s for zero output = dead runtime) and slow kill (300s for no LLM activity = stalled provider)
- Extracts `_watchdog_kill()` for reuse by both phases

## Context

After the v1.3.17 regression (Cloudflare provider init hang, confirmed with `--pure` flag), we need defense-in-depth against future OpenCode runtime regressions:

1. **Canary** catches broken runtimes before any worker is dispatched. Cached for 30 min (one test per pulse cycle). Uses `--pure` and haiku for speed (~5-10s).
2. **Phase 1 watchdog** (30s) kills workers that produce zero output — runtime didn't even start. Previously these burned 300s before getting killed.
3. **Phase 2 watchdog** (300s) is the existing behavior for workers that started but stalled on API calls.

## Files changed

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:2025-2090` — new `_run_canary_test()` function
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:2206-2220` — canary gate in `cmd_run()`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1370-1423` — two-phase `_run_activity_watchdog()` + extracted `_watchdog_kill()`

title: GH#17629: fix url-allowlist-check grep -c double-output corrupts GITHUB_OUTPUT
body:
## Summary

- Fix `grep -c` + `|| echo "0"` double-output bug in URL Allowlist Check workflow that corrupts `GITHUB_OUTPUT` on every PR with no unknown URLs (the happy path)
- One-character change: `|| echo "0"` → `|| true` on line 106

## Root Cause

When `grep -c` finds no matches, it outputs `0` to stdout AND exits with code 1. The `|| echo "0"` fallback fires inside the command substitution, appending a second `0`. Result: `UNKNOWN_COUNT="0\n0"` — a two-line string instead of an integer.

This breaks:
1. `[[ "$UNKNOWN_COUNT" -eq 0 ]]` — bash can't compare multiline string as integer
2. `echo "unknown_count=${UNKNOWN_COUNT}"` writes a bare `0` line to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (invalid format)
3. Status description becomes garbled: `"Maintainer PR: 0\n0 new URL(s)"`

## Evidence

Failed run: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/24052917718/job/70152584892?pr=17627

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level**: Low (CI workflow config, no runtime code)
- **Verification**: `self-assessed` — the fix is a well-understood bash pattern; verification will be the next PR that triggers this workflow

Closes #17629

title: GH#17632: fix nesting-only violations creating false-positive simplification issues
body:
## Summary

Fixes a false-positive in the complexity scan that created issues titled "0 functions >100 lines" — a misleading and unactionable result.

## Root Cause

`_scan_shell_files` in `complexity-scan-helper.sh` includes a file in scan output when **either**:
- `long_func_count >= COMPLEXITY_FILE_VIOLATION_THRESHOLD` (function length violation), OR
- `max_nesting > COMPLEXITY_NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` (nesting depth violation)

When only the nesting condition triggers, `long_func_count=0`. This value flows into `_complexity_scan_create_issues` as `violation_count`, which uses it verbatim in the issue title and body:

```
simplification: reduce function complexity in .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh (0 functions >100 lines)
```

This is factually correct (0 violations) but creates a real issue that gets dispatched to workers who find nothing to fix.

**Verified on dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:**
- Long functions (>100 lines): **0**
- Max nesting depth: **9** (threshold: 8) ← this triggered the issue

## Fix

Added a guard in `_complexity_scan_create_issues` to skip entries where `violation_count=0`. These are nesting-only violations; the current issue template is function-length-specific and cannot meaningfully describe them.

```bash
if [[ "${violation_count:-0}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] Complexity scan: skipping ${file_path} — nesting-only violation (0 long functions)" >>""
    issues_skipped=$((issues_skipped + 1))
    continue
fi
```

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — added nesting-only skip guard in `_complexity_scan_create_issues`

## Testing

- `bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — syntax check passes
- ShellCheck on the modified block — no violations
- Logic verified: `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` has 0 long functions and nesting=9, would now be skipped

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level: Low** — guard condition added to issue creation loop; no behavior change for files with actual function length violations.

Closes #17632

title: fix: use SHA-keyed concurrency group on main to prevent badge cancellation
body:
## Summary

The Code Quality Analysis badge intermittently shows "failing" despite all checks passing. Root cause: rapid pushes to `main` (from pulse auto-merges) cause queued workflow runs to be cancelled, and GitHub badges treat "cancelled" as "failing".

## Root Cause

GitHub's concurrency queue holds only **one pending run per group**. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects in-progress runs, but when a third push arrives while a second is queued, the queued run is **always replaced** — regardless of `cancel-in-progress`. The replaced run completes with `conclusion: cancelled`, which the badge renders as failing.

Evidence from last 20 main-branch runs: 4 cancellations, all following rapid successive pushes within 10-20 seconds (pulse auto-merges). Cancelled runs had zero jobs — never ran, just evicted from the queue.

## Fix

Key each main push by SHA so they never share a concurrency group:

```yaml
# Before
group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

# After
group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.sha || github.ref }}
```

- **Main pushes**: group = `Code Quality Analysis-<sha>` — independent, no cancellations
- **PR pushes**: group = `Code Quality Analysis-refs/heads/<branch>` — new push cancels stale run (unchanged, desirable)

## Trade-off

Slightly more CI minutes on main (parallel runs instead of queued). Given the pulse merges rapidly, each merge should validate independently anyway.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: Low (CI config only, no application code)
- **Verification**: self-assessed — the fix is a well-documented GitHub Actions concurrency pattern

title: GH#17648: try continuation before killing stalled workers with activity
body:
## Summary

- **What**: When the watchdog kills a worker that had prior LLM activity (stream drop mid-session), try resuming the session up to 2 times before falling through to provider rotation
- **Why**: Workers that created worktrees, read files, and partially implemented changes lose all that context when killed and restarted from scratch on a different provider. A continuation prompt preserves the session.
- **How**: New exit code 78 (`watchdog_stall_continue`) distinguishes "stall with activity" from "dead on arrival" (exit 124 with no activity). The retry loop handles 78 like premature exit (77) but with a dedicated counter capped at 2.

Closes #17648

## Flow

```
Watchdog detects stall (300s no output growth)
  → kills worker process
  → _handle_run_result checks: had activity?
    → YES: store session ID, return 78
      → retry loop: resume session with continuation prompt
      → try up to 2 times
      → if still failing: fall through to provider rotation
    → NO: return rate_limit (existing behavior)
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` | `_handle_run_result`: exit 124 + activity → return 78 with session ID stored. `cmd_run`: handle exit 78 with `watchdog_continue_count` (max 2), dedicated continuation prompt explaining the connection drop. |

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level**: High (retry loop, session lifecycle)
- **Verification**: `self-assessed` — no headless dispatch environment for end-to-end testing
- **ShellCheck**: Clean (SC1091 info only)

## Key decisions

- **Separate counter (max 2)**: Watchdog stalls get 2 continuation attempts (not 10 like premature exits). Stream drops that keep recurring indicate a deeper issue — don't waste tokens on repeated resumption.
- **Different prompt**: The continuation prompt tells the model its connection dropped and prior work is on disk, rather than the premature-exit prompt which assumes the model stopped voluntarily.
- **Falls through to provider rotation**: After 2 failed continuations, the existing `_cmd_run_prepare_retry` logic takes over (may switch models/providers).

title: GH#17648: workers self-report failures for immediate tier escalation
body:
## Summary

- Workers now write to the fast-fail counter on exit, triggering tier escalation (standard to reasoning) immediately instead of waiting 60-90+ minutes for the pulse to discover the failure
- Sources `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` for `escalate_issue_tier()`; counter write uses the same atomic JSON + mkdir lock as pulse-wrapper and worker-watchdog

Related: #17648

## Problem

```
Worker fails → _cmd_run_finish('fail') → releases claim → exits
           ↑ DOES NOT write fast-fail counter

...30 min passes...

Pulse discovers orphan → fast_fail_record() → count=1
...30 more min...
Next failure discovered → count=2 → escalate_issue_tier() → tier:reasoning
```

Evidence: #17642 had 3 sonnet dispatches over 67 minutes, counter only reached 1. #17643 had 3 gpt-5.3-codex dispatches, counter had no entry at all.

## Fix

```
Worker fails → _cmd_run_finish('fail')
  → _release_dispatch_claim (existing)
  → _report_failure_to_fast_fail (NEW)
    → atomic read/increment/write of fast-fail-counter.json
```

title: GH#17642: stop auto-closing issues from main-commit check false positives
body:
## Summary

Remove `gh issue close` from both the dispatch guard (`_is_task_committed_to_main` at line 6772) and the conflicting-PR merge pass (`_close_conflicting_pr` at line 8877). The commit search has too many false positives to safely auto-close issues.

Issues #17642 and #17643 were falsely closed **5+ times each** by both the `marcusquinn` and `alex-solovyev` runners despite no work being merged. The `robstiles` runner even posted a detailed analysis confirming the function `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer()` does not exist on main.

- **False close** (issue closed with no work merged): destructive, needs manual reopen, loses dispatch context, wastes cycles

title: GH#17674: fix daemon stacking in memory-pressure-monitor.sh
body:
## Summary

Replace the TOCTOU-vulnerable PID file guard in `cmd_daemon()` with an atomic `mkdir`-based lock that prevents multiple daemon instances from stacking when launchd triggers fire within the same second.

Closes #17674

## Changes

- **`cmd_daemon()`**: Atomic `mkdir` lock with PID written inside lock dir. Write failures are surfaced (no more swallowed `2>/dev/null`). Legacy PID file still written for backward compatibility with `cmd_stop`/`cmd_status`.
- **`cmd_stop()`**: Checks lock dir first, falls back to legacy PID file. Cleans up both on stop.
- **`cmd_uninstall()`**: Cleans up lock directory alongside state files.
- **`_status_print_os_and_config()`**: Checks lock dir for daemon PID, falls back to legacy PID file.
- **`cmd_install()`**: `StartInterval` increased from 30s to 300s (5 minutes) to reduce trigger frequency.
- **Help text**: Updated to reflect lock mechanism and new interval.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: **Low** (daemon lock mechanism, no user-facing features, no data paths)
- `bash -n` syntax check: pass
- `shellcheck`: zero violations
- `grep -c lockdir`: 4 references (expected 3+)
- `grep 'Failed to write PID'`: 1 match (error surfaced, not swallowed)

## Key Decisions

- Kept legacy PID file write in `cmd_daemon()` for backward compatibility — existing `cmd_stop` invocations from older deployed versions will still work during the transition.
- Used `mkdir` over `flock` for portability (macOS bash 3.2 compatibility, no external deps).
- `StartInterval` changed from 30s to 300s per issue guidance to reduce launchd trigger frequency.

title: t1907: fix gh-signature-helper.sh runtime guard for OpenCode DB queries
body:
## Summary

- Gate all OpenCode DB queries behind `_is_opencode_runtime()` to prevent reading stale session data when running in Claude Code or other runtimes
- Add `_detect_claude_code_model()` fallback that reads `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` / `CLAUDE_MODEL` env vars for Claude Code sessions
- Add Claude Code session type inference from `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS` and `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS` env vars

## Problem

`gh-signature-helper.sh` unconditionally queries the OpenCode SQLite DB (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) for model, tokens, session time, and session type. When running in Claude Code, this DB may still exist on disk from a previous OpenCode session, causing the signature footer to display the wrong model (e.g., `gpt-5.4-pro` from an old OpenCode session instead of the actual Claude model).

## Solution

Added `_is_opencode_runtime()` guard function that checks:
1. `OPENCODE=1` env var (fast path)
2. Parent process chain for "opencode" (fallback)

All six functions that query the OpenCode DB are now gated behind this check:
- `_detect_session_model()` — falls back to `_detect_claude_code_model()`
- `_detect_session_tokens_with_since()` — returns empty (no DB to query)
- `_detect_session_time()` — returns empty
- `_detect_session_type()` — infers from env vars (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `CLAUDE_CODE`)
- `_sum_child_tokens()` — skips auto-detect of parent session
- `cmd_record_child()` — skips auto-detect of parent session and child tokens

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: **Low** (shell script, no state changes, signature footer only)
- ShellCheck: clean (only SC1091 info for sourced file)
- Existing test suite: 50/55 pass (same 5 pre-existing failures on main)
- Manual verification: `_is_opencode_runtime()` correctly detects OpenCode in current env; `_detect_claude_code_model()` correctly reads `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`

title: GH#17699: fix _ts_to_epoch() timezone bug causing premature stale recovery
body:
## Summary

- `_ts_to_epoch()` on macOS stripped the `Z` suffix from UTC timestamps then passed them to `date -j -f`, which interprets input as **local time**. On any machine east of UTC this made every GitHub timestamp appear `TZ_OFFSET` seconds older than reality.
- On BST (UTC+1), a 20-second-old dispatch claim computed as 3620s — exceeding the 1800s threshold — causing stale recovery to immediately kill freshly dispatched workers.
- Fix: prefix `TZ=UTC` on the macOS `date` call. Linux branch (`date -d`) is unaffected.

## Evidence

GH#17699 comment timeline:
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 17:20:55Z | `DISPATCH_CLAIM` posted |
| 17:21:17Z | Worker dispatched (PID 3349956) |
| 17:21:20Z | Stale recovery fires — reports "3620s old" (3600s TZ offset + 20s actual age) |

## Verification

```bash
# Before fix (BST):
_ts_to_epoch "2026-04-07T17:20:55Z"  # Returns epoch of 17:20:55 BST = 16:20:55 UTC (wrong)

# After fix:
_ts_to_epoch "2026-04-07T17:20:55Z"  # Returns epoch of 17:20:55 UTC (correct)
```

ShellCheck clean.

Closes #17699

title: GH#17707: add merge pass observability logging and UNKNOWN retry
body:
## Summary

The deterministic merge pass silently dropped PRs that hit any of 5 `continue` conditions — zero log output when a PR was skipped. This made it impossible to diagnose why ready-to-merge PRs sat idle for hours.

**Root cause of the throughput stall**: The dedup false positive (fixed in #17715) blocked dispatch, but the merge pass *also* failed to merge the fix PRs for multiple cycles with no trace in logs. Investigation showed every skip condition was a silent `continue`.

## Changes

- **Diagnostic logging**: Every skip reason now logs to `pulse.log` with PR number, repo, and reason
  - `mergeable != MERGEABLE` (including UNKNOWN)
  - `reviewDecision = CHANGES_REQUESTED`
  - Non-collaborator author
  - Workflow file modifications without token scope
  - Linked issue has `needs-maintainer-review`
- **UNKNOWN mergeability retry**: GitHub returns `UNKNOWN` for recently-pushed PRs while computing merge status. The merge pass now retries once after 5s instead of silently skipping for the entire cycle
- **Always log summary**: The merge pass now logs `merged=0, closed_conflicting=0, failed=0` even when nothing happened (previously only logged when merged+closed > 0, hiding zero-throughput cycles)

## Self-healing impact

Before: PRs could be silently skipped for hours with no diagnostic trace. Debugging required manual reproduction of the exact merge pass logic.

After: Every skipped PR explains why in `pulse.log`. UNKNOWN mergeability self-heals with a retry. Zero-throughput cycles are visible in logs.

Closes #17707

title: GH#17726: replace while-read loop with awk in _read_brief_what_section
body:
## Summary

Addresses gemini review feedback from PR #17693 on `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`.

The `_read_brief_what_section` function used a `while read` loop to extract the `## What` section from brief files, building a multi-line string in a variable. This is replaced with a single `awk` command that streams output directly — more idiomatic and performant for parsing file content in shell.

## Changes

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:709-726` — replaced 15-line while-read loop + sed trim with 1-line awk pipeline

## Before

```bash
local in_what=false
local what_content=
while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ "$line" =~ ^##[[:space:]]+[Ww]hat ]]; then
        in_what=true
        continue
    fi
    if [[ "$in_what" == "true" ]]; then
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^## ]]; then
            break
        fi
        what_content="${what_content}${line}"$'\n'
    fi
done <"$brief_file"
what_content=$(printf '%s' "$what_content" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
```

## After

```bash
local what_content
what_content=$(awk '/^##[[:space:]]+[Ww]hat/ {f=1; next} /^##/ {f=0} f' "$brief_file" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
```

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level**: Low — shell script refactor with identical output semantics. No runtime environment needed.

**Verification**: shellcheck passes (SC1091 info finding is pre-existing, unrelated to this change). Logic equivalence verified by manual trace: awk sets flag on `## What` header, clears on next `##` header, prints flagged lines — identical to the loop behaviour.

Closes #17726

title: GH#17707: reasoning-tier enrichment for failed worker issues
body:
## Summary

When workers fail on an issue, the pulse currently just backs off and re-dispatches with the same brief — which often fails again for the same reason. This adds an intermediate step: spawn a reasoning-tier (opus) worker to analyze the codebase and enrich the issue body with concrete implementation guidance before re-dispatch.

## Problem

Workers fail when issue bodies lack implementation context (specific file paths, reference patterns, verification commands). The existing `_escalate_body_quality_gate` detects this but only posts a diagnostic comment — it doesn't fix the problem. Re-dispatching a more expensive model (tier escalation) wastes tokens on the same exploration problem.

## Solution

**New self-healing flow:**
```
dispatch → worker fails → fast_fail_record sets enrichment_needed=true →
next cycle: dispatch_enrichment_workers spawns reasoning analyst →
analyst reads issue + kill comments + searches codebase →
appends "## Worker Guidance" to issue body (file paths, patterns, verification) →
marks enrichment_done → next dispatch uses enriched context
```

**Key design decisions:**
- **Reasoning tier only** — lesser tiers risk compounding the same blind spots that caused the failure
- **Max 2 per cycle** — same rate limit as triage reviews
- **One-shot** — enrichment runs once per issue; if it still fails, normal tier escalation handles it
- **Inline execution** — runs in the fill floor stage (after triage, before implementation dispatch), not as a background worker

## Changes

- `_fast_fail_record_locked()`: Sets `enrichment_needed=true` in fast-fail state on first non-rate-limit failure
- `dispatch_enrichment_workers()`: New function (modeled on `dispatch_triage_reviews`) that processes flagged issues with inline reasoning analysis
- `_ff_mark_enrichment_done()`: Clears the enrichment flag after processing
- `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor()`: Integrates enrichment stage between triage and implementation dispatch

Closes #17707

* **New Features**
  * Added automated enrichment stage that generates AI-powered worker guidance for issues by analyzing context and appending recommendations.

* **Chores**

  * Improved state management with enrichment status tracking and completion flags.

title: GH#17707: check open PRs in dedup Layer 4 — prevent duplicate dispatch
body:
## Summary

`has_open_pr()` only checked `--state merged` PRs. Open PRs were invisible to the entire 7-layer dedup system. When a worker created PRs and then its dispatch comment TTL expired (30 min), the pulse dispatched another worker for the same issue — wasting tokens on duplicate work.

**Evidence:** Issue #17707 — alex-solovyev's worker created PRs #17711 and #17714 (both open). 5 minutes later, marcusquinn's pulse dispatched a third worker that created PR #17715.

## Root cause

Layer 4 (`has_open_pr`) searched `gh pr list --state merged` exclusively. The function name says "open" but it only checked merged. No other layer compensated — Layer 5 (dispatch comment) had expired, Layer 6 (assignee) was cleared by claim release.

## Fix

Add open PR check as the first step in `has_open_pr()`:
- Fetches open PRs via `gh pr list --state open`
- Matches by `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #NNN` in body OR `GH#NNN`/`#NNN` in title
- Blocks dispatch if a matching open PR exists

Falls through to existing merged PR check if no open match found.

Closes #17707

title: GH#17707: dedup checks commit messages — closing keywords go in commits not PR bodies
body:
## Summary

Shifts the closing keyword convention from PR bodies to commit messages and updates the dedup system to match. PR bodies describe intent; commits describe work done. The dedup system should check what was actually done.

## Problem

A PR body saying `Closes #123` doesn't mean the PR solves #123 — it might reference it for context, or the worker might have failed to implement it. This caused both false-positive dedup blocks (PR mentions issue but doesn't solve it) and false-negative blocks (PR #17749 fix checked PR bodies, which are unreliable).

## Changes

- **Convention (build.txt)**: Closing keywords (`Closes #NNN`) go in commit messages, not PR bodies. PR bodies use `For #NNN` or `Implements #NNN` for context.
- **Open PR dedup**: Scans `commits[].messageHeadline` for closing keywords instead of PR body text. Also matches `GH#NNN`/`#NNN` in PR titles.
- **Merged PR check**: Kept as-is for backward compatibility (existing merged PRs have keywords in bodies).
- **GitHub auto-close**: Works from commit messages on merge to default branch — no behavior change.

For #17707

title: GH#17746: add triage dedup guard to prevent repeated lock/unlock cycles
body:
## Summary

- Add content-hash dedup to `dispatch_triage_reviews()` — prevents the same NMR issue from being re-triaged every pulse cycle when content hasn't changed
- Make `unlock_issue_after_worker()` symmetric with `lock_issue_for_worker()` — only lock/unlock NMR issues, preventing spurious timeline events
- Re-triage triggers correctly when the issue author edits the body or adds new comments

## Problem

Issue #17746 had **5 lock/unlock cycles in 50 minutes** with zero useful work done. Each pulse cycle: lock → run triage agent → agent produces no usable output → unlock → repeat. This wasted tokens, API calls, and polluted the issue timeline visible to the external reporter.

Root cause: `dispatch_triage_reviews()` had no dedup guard — the triage state file is regenerated each cycle, and the issue remains NMR-labeled (only cryptographic approval can remove it), so it was picked up every time.

## Changes

1. **Content-hash dedup** (`_triage_content_hash`, `_triage_is_cached`, `_triage_update_cache`): SHA-256 of issue body + human comments (excludes `github-actions[bot]` and `## Review:` comments). Cached at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/triage-cache/`. On cache hit → skip. On miss → triage → cache.

2. **Fetch restructuring**: Body + comments fetched first (shared by dedup check and prefetch prompt). Remaining API calls (PR diff, closed issues, git log) only run on cache miss — saving 3-4 API calls per skipped issue.

3. **Symmetric unlock guard**: `unlock_issue_after_worker()` now checks `issue_was_ever_nmr` before calling `gh issue unlock`, matching the existing guard in `lock_issue_for_worker()`.

## Re-triage triggers

- Author edits the issue body → hash changes → re-triage
- Author or contributor adds a new comment → hash changes → re-triage
- Bot comments and our own review comments are excluded from the hash → no loops

Closes #17746

title: t1919: fix: resolve_api_key subshell export bug in model-availability-helper.sh
body:
## Summary

Fixes the subshell export bug in `resolve_api_key()` that caused headless dispatch to fail in clean environments.

**Root cause:** `resolve_api_key()` previously echoed the variable *name* (not the value) and relied on `export` side-effects to populate the environment for `_get_key_value()`. When called inside a `$()` subshell (as `probe_provider()` does at L809), the `export` never reached the parent shell. `_get_key_value()` then found the variable empty and returned exit 3 ("Key var found but empty"), blocking all headless dispatch.

**Fix:**
- `resolve_api_key()` now echoes the key value directly (all three sources: env, gopass, credentials.sh)
- `probe_provider()` uses a single `api_key=$(resolve_api_key "$provider")` call — no separate `_get_key_value()` needed
- `_get_key_value()` kept as a deprecated shim delegating to `resolve_api_key` for backward compatibility
- Security comment updated: callers must capture in `local` vars and must not log the value

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` — `resolve_api_key()`, `_get_key_value()`, `probe_provider()`

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level:** Medium (API key resolution, headless dispatch path)

Self-assessed — the fix follows standard shell idiom (functions echo values, callers capture via `$()`). The logic change is mechanical: replace `echo "$var_name"` with `echo "${!var_name}"` and remove the two-step resolve+get pattern.

Verification command from issue:
```bash
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" bash --norc --noprofile -c \
  'source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh; api_key=$(resolve_api_key "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"); echo "length: ${#api_key}"'
```
Should show non-zero length when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in gopass or credentials.sh.

- **Why `Resolves`**: PR body closing keywords only auto-close issues on *merge* (not on PR creation), so there was never a risk of premature closure. The original rule over-reached from a valid concern about planning commits.

- EDIT: `.agents/tools/autoagent/autoagent.md` — PR template `Closes #` → `Resolves #`

title: t1927: fix infinite dispatch loops — stale recovery fast-fail, dispatch cap, blocked-by enforcement
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause of infinite dispatch loops where issues were dispatched 10+ times in 6 hours with 0 PRs produced (observed on GH#17700, GH#17701, GH#17702, GH#17695).

## Changes

### Fix 1: Stale recovery records fast-fail (pulse-wrapper.sh:6523-6532)
When `_is_stale_assignment()` recovers a silent worker timeout, the dedup helper outputs `STALE_RECOVERED`. The Layer 6 integration now detects this and calls `fast_fail_record()` with reason `stale_timeout`. Previously, silent timeouts bypassed the fast-fail counter — it stayed at 0 while issues looped indefinitely.

### Fix 2: Dispatch count cap (pulse-wrapper.sh:8387-8451)
New `dispatch_count_exceeded()` function counts total `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments on an issue. At the cap (default 8, configurable via `DISPATCH_COUNT_CAP`), labels the issue `stuck` and posts a diagnostic comment. Independent safety valve that works regardless of fast-fail counter state.

### Fix 3: Blocked-by enforcement (pulse-wrapper.sh:8453-8519)
New `is_blocked_by_unresolved()` function parses issue bodies for `blocked-by:tNNN` and `Blocked by #NNN` patterns. Checks whether the blocking task/issue is still open. Issue #17701 explicitly stated "Blocked by t1910" but was dispatched 8 times because the pulse never parsed dependency constraints.

title: t1927: escalate tier before stuck label, fix squash-merge regex false positive
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #17780 — fixes two issues preventing dispatch progress.

### Fix 1: Escalate tier before labeling stuck

`dispatch_count_exceeded()` now checks the current tier label before blocking. If the issue hasn't been tried at `tier:reasoning`, it calls `escalate_issue_tier()` and resets fast-fail instead of labeling `stuck`. Only issues that have exhausted `tier:reasoning` get the `stuck` label.

**Before**: 8 standard-tier dispatches → stuck (never tried reasoning)
**After**: 8 standard-tier dispatches → escalate to reasoning → 8 reasoning-tier dispatches → stuck

### Fix 2: Escape squash-merge regex parens

`_is_task_committed_to_main` used `(#NNN)` as a search pattern with `-E` (extended regex). Unescaped parens are capture groups, so the pattern matched bare `#NNN` anywhere in commit bodies — including evidence tables and PR descriptions. Changed to `\(#NNN\)` to match only the literal GitHub squash-merge suffix.

**Impact**: #17700, #17701, #17702 were blocked because PR #17780 body contained `#17700` etc. in the root cause analysis table.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level**: Medium (dispatch logic, regex)
- **Testing**: Self-assessed — both changes are narrow, additive fixes to existing guard logic.

Resolves #17777

title: GH#17790: fix(opencode-plugin) strip trailing assistant messages to prevent Claude 4.x prefill error
body:
## Summary

Adds a defensive plugin-level guard that strips trailing assistant messages from the outgoing LLM payload, preventing the "This model does not support assistant message prefill" error on Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.x — most often hit on the mobile webui.

## Why

Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.x (Anthropic native, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex) reject any conversation that ends with an assistant message:

> This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.

opencode v1.3.17 / v1.4.0 has a partial gate at `session/prompt.ts` (`lastAssistant2?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(...)`) that handles the most common continuation case, but it **fails open** when `finish` is `undefined` — which is exactly the state left by aborted/interrupted previous turns. Mobile users hit this constantly because flaky connections cause aborts.

Three upstream PRs ([sst/opencode#14772](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/14772), [#16921](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16921), [#18091](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/18091)) all fix this in `provider/transform.ts` by adding `stripTrailingAssistant()`. None are merged.

## What

- **NEW** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/prefill-guard.mjs` — pure module exporting `createPrefillGuardHook(deps)`. Strips trailing assistant messages from `output.messages` only when **safe**:
  - Preserves messages with `finish === "tool-calls"`
  - Preserves messages with active tool parts (`pending` / `running` / `completed`)
  - Strips assistants whose tool parts are all in `error` / `aborted` state, or that have no tool parts
- **EDIT** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — imports the guard and composes it into the `experimental.chat.messages.transform` hook **after** the existing `messagesTransformHook` so TTSR's rule scanning still sees all assistants before they're stripped.

## Safety properties

- **Session DB is never modified** — stripped messages still display in transcript history. Only the outgoing LLM payload is altered.
- **Tool-call flows preserved** — assistants with live tool calls are never stripped. Only assistants whose tool parts are all in terminal error/aborted states (or that have no tool parts at all) are eligible.
- **Never throws** — wrapped in try/catch with diagnostic logging via `qualityLog`. A bug here cannot break the hook chain.
- **Provider-agnostic** — works for Anthropic native, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex, and any other path that hits this hook.
- **Composition order matters**: TTSR runs first because it scans the last 3 assistants for rule violations and may append a synthetic user correction (which itself fixes the user-final invariant). The guard runs second so anything TTSR didn't append a correction for still gets stripped.

## Verification

```bash
# Syntax check both files
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/prefill-guard.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs

# Restart and verify clean plugin load
systemctl --user restart opencode-web.service
journalctl --user -u opencode-web.service --since "now" | grep -iE "aidevops|fail|exception"

# Confirm guard fires when stripping (only on actual triggering message)
journalctl --user -u opencode-web.service -f | grep prefill-guard
```

The fix has been deployed and verified locally — opencode-web restarted cleanly, plugin loaded without errors, and the mobile webui has been working since.

## Related upstream

- anomalyco/opencode#13768 — original bug report
- anomalyco/opencode#17982 — continuation loop root cause analysis
- anomalyco/opencode#14772 — fix PR (open)
- anomalyco/opencode#16921 — alternate fix PR (open)
- anomalyco/opencode#18091 — bundled fix PR (open)

This plugin-level guard is a workaround until one of those upstream PRs lands. When they do, this guard becomes a no-op (the upstream strip will happen first) and can optionally be removed.

Resolves #17790

title: t1927: remove arbitrary dispatch count cap — let fast-fail + escalation drive progression
body:
## Summary

Removes the `dispatch_count_exceeded()` function and `DISPATCH_COUNT_CAP` config entirely. The hard cap was an arbitrary limit that gave up on issues instead of solving them.

### What remains (and works)

The dispatch system already has the right progression mechanisms:

1. **fast_fail with exponential backoff** — gives breathing room between attempts (10m → 20m → 40m → ... → 7d max)
2. **escalate_issue_tier** — moves to higher-capability models after consecutive failures at a tier
3. **stale recovery records fast-fail** — silent worker timeouts now count as failures and feed into backoff + escalation (from earlier in this session, PR #17780)
4. **blocked-by enforcement** — skips genuinely blocked work (from PR #17780)

Together, these ensure the system keeps trying with progressively more capable models and longer backoff intervals. Issues that are genuinely hard get escalated to reasoning-tier models. Issues with systemic blockers (bad auth, missing context) hit the fast-fail threshold and enter long backoff naturally.

### What was wrong with the cap

1. Too low (8) — didn't allow enough attempts across tier escalation
2. Arbitrary — not based on any analysis of what number leads to success vs waste
3. Labels "stuck" instead of solving — defers to human input when the diagnostic data is already available to the system
4. The system already ran months of productive high-concurrency worker dispatch without any cap

For #17777

title: GH#17779: fix _is_task_committed_to_main subject-only matching for tNNN/GH#NNN
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Layer 3 false positive in `_is_task_committed_to_main()`: `git --grep` searches the entire commit message (subject + body), so body cross-references like `(t101)` in code commits permanently block dispatch for unrelated tasks.

## Root Cause

`git log --grep="t101"` matches any commit whose message contains `t101` anywhere — including documentation cross-references in commit bodies. The existing two-stage filter (subject-line prefix + path-based planning detection) cannot catch this because the commit has a legitimate non-planning subject and touches real code files.

## Fix

Split `search_patterns` into two arrays by match scope:

- **`subject_patterns`** (Patterns 1 & 2: `tNNN`, `GH#NNN`): use `--format '%H %s'` + `grep -wE` for subject-only matching. Body cross-references are invisible to `%s` format. `grep -w` also prevents substring collisions (`t101` matching `t1010`).
- **`message_patterns`** (Patterns 3-5: squash-merge suffix, `Closes`/`Fixes`): keep using `--grep` (full message) — closing keywords legitimately appear in commit bodies.

Extract the path-based planning filter into `_count_impl_commits()` helper to avoid duplicating the two-stage filter logic across both loops.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `_is_task_committed_to_main()` function (~6724-6876)

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations on the modified function
- Logic verified: `grep -wE "t101"` on `'%H %s'` output correctly matches `t101` in subjects, does not match `t1010` (word boundary), and body cross-references are not present in `%s` format output
- Permutation audit from issue: gaps 6 (body cross-ref) and 7 (substring collision) are now addressed

title: GH#440: fix setup.sh blocking on generate-skills.sh (56s → 0.2s)

## Summary

- `setup.sh` was blocking for **56 seconds** on every run because `generate-skills.sh` unconditionally regenerated all 957 SKILL.md files from 1650 source `.md` files
- Root cause: ~3000 subprocess spawns (`awk`, `grep`, `mkdir`, file writes) with no caching

2. Compare to stored hash in `~/.aidevops/agents/.skills-source-hash`
3. Match + SKILL.md files exist → exit immediately
4. Mismatch → regenerate all, write new hash

Cache invalidates automatically when any source `.md` file is added, removed, resized, or modified.

`extract_failure_signature()` calls `gh run view --log-failed` to get the error text from a failed CI run. This returns empty when:
- Run logs have expired (GitHub retains logs for 90 days, but the miner may run after expiry)
- The run is still in progress when the miner fires
- API rate limiting

When empty, the function returned the literal string `no_failed_log_output` as the signature. This caused the failure miner to cluster all such events under a single vague signature, producing unhelpful systemic-failure issues (like #17809 itself) that don't identify the actual error.

## Fix

Added a two-step fallback inside `extract_failure_signature()`:
1. `GET /actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` — find the first job with `conclusion=failure`
2. `GET /actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs` — get that job's log output directly

Both API calls are wrapped in `2>/dev/null || true` so failures are non-fatal. If the fallback also returns empty, the function still returns `no_failed_log_output` as before.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-failure-miner-helper.sh` — `extract_failure_signature()` function (lines 164-193)

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: **Low** — non-fatal fallback path, both API calls wrapped in `|| true`
- Testing: ShellCheck zero violations on modified file; logic verified against GitHub Actions API docs

Resolves #17809

title: GH#17804: fix upgrade-planning template placeholder extraction
body:
## Summary

Resolves #17804

`aidevops upgrade-planning` extracted template example lines (tXXX/tYYY/tZZZ) from the `## Format` section as real tasks during v1.0→v1.1 TODO.md migration, polluting the Backlog with bogus placeholder tasks.

## Changes

### 1. Section-aware parser (`aidevops.sh:_upgrade_todo`)
The awk extraction now tracks `## Format` section boundaries and markdown code block fences. Lines inside either are skipped during extraction.

### 2. ID validator (`aidevops.sh:_upgrade_todo`)
After extraction, a second awk pass filters task lines to only keep those with numeric IDs matching `^t[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$`. This rejects `tXXX`, `tYYY`, `tZZZ`, and any other non-numeric ID patterns. Non-task lines (subsection headers, comments, blank lines) are preserved.

### 3. Template hardening (`.agents/templates/todo-template.md`)
Format examples are now wrapped in an HTML comment block (`<!-- ... -->`) so they are invisible to any line-based parser. A single-line format reference replaces the code block for human-readable documentation.

## Files changed

- `aidevops.sh` — `_upgrade_todo()` function: section-aware extraction + ID validator
- `.agents/templates/todo-template.md` — format examples wrapped in HTML comments
- `tests/test-upgrade-planning-placeholders.sh` — 12-assertion regression test

- **Risk level**: Medium (planning tool, no auth/payment/data-deletion)

- **Verification**: `bash tests/test-upgrade-planning-placeholders.sh --verbose` → 12 passed, 0 failed

## Key decisions

- Applied belt-and-braces: both section-aware parsing AND ID validation, so either defense alone prevents the bug
- Kept format examples in HTML comments rather than removing them entirely — preserves documentation for source readers
- ID validator uses positive matching (`t[0-9]+`) rather than negative matching (rejecting specific placeholders) — more defensive against future non-numeric patterns

title: t1913: automate ratchet-down of complexity thresholds
body:
## Summary

Implements automated ratchet-down of complexity thresholds (t1913). Thresholds have only gone UP (11 bumps documented in comments) — this closes the loop so simplification wins translate into tighter CI gates.

## Changes

### `.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh`

Added `cmd_ratchet_check()` command that:
- Reads current thresholds from `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf`
- Counts actual violations using the same awk/grep logic as CI
- Covers all four ratchetable thresholds: `FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD`, `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD`, `FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD`, `BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD`
- Outputs proposed new thresholds (actual + 2 buffer) when gap >= configured minimum (default 5)
- Returns exit 0 when ratchet-down is possible, exit 1 when thresholds are already tight
- Added to main dispatch case and help text

### `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`

Added Phase 5 after simplification backfill:
- Calls `complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check` after backfill so closed issues are reflected
- When ratchet-down is available, creates a `chore: ratchet-down complexity thresholds` issue with worker guidance
- Deduplicates by checking for existing open ratchet-down PRs before creating a new issue

## Testing

```bash
# Command exists and runs
.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check . 5
# Output:
# [complexity-scan] INFO: Actual violations — func:28 nest:256 size:52 bash32:71
# [complexity-scan] INFO: Current thresholds — func:420 nest:262 size:53 bash32:72
# FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD: 420 → 30 (actual: 28, gap: 392)
# NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD: 262 → 258 (actual: 256, gap: 6)
# [complexity-scan] INFO: Ratchet-down available: 2 threshold(s) can be lowered

# Exit 1 when gap too small
.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check . 500
# [complexity-scan] INFO: No ratchet-down available: all thresholds within gap of 500

# ShellCheck clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/complexity-scan-helper.sh
```

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Low** — docs/config/agent prompts pattern. New command added to existing script; no changes to existing logic. Pulse integration is best-effort (|| true) and creates issues, not PRs directly.

## Key Decisions

- Buffer of +2 above actual count prevents flapping from concurrent PRs
- Gap threshold of 5 prevents noise — only propose when meaningful reduction accumulated
- Ratchet-check is idempotent — running twice with no changes produces same proposal
- Pulse integration creates an issue (not a PR directly) to keep the ratchet-down in the normal review flow
- ShellCheck OOM on pulse-wrapper.sh (12K lines) is a pre-existing limitation; the added section follows existing patterns

## Summary

Add a new `qlty-smells` job to `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` that runs `qlty smells` in diff mode on PRs. Fails if the PR introduces new code smells, preventing maintainability grade regression.

Resolves #17700

## Changes

- **NEW job**: `qlty-smells` in `code-quality.yml`, positioned after `complexity-check` and before `sonarcloud`
- PR-only gate (`if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`) — diff mode needs a comparison base
- Installs Qlty CLI via `https://qlty.sh/install`

- **Diff mode, not `--all`**: Only blocks new smells. The existing 224+ smells would fail every PR if we used `--all`.
- **PR-only**: Main-branch pushes don't need this gate — they're already merged.
- **Hard gate** (`continue-on-error: false` default): This is a blocking check, not advisory.
- **Inherits `.qlty/qlty.toml` config**: Exclude patterns, test patterns, and plugins are already configured.

title: GH#17829: Fix headless dispatch when opencode serve is running + triage failure visibility
body:
## Summary

Resolves #17829

Three fixes for headless worker dispatch and triage visibility:

1. **Bug 1 — Missing plugin dependency**: Added `@bufbuild/protobuf` to `opencode-aidevops` plugin `dependencies` in `package.json`. Updated `agent-deploy.sh` to verify the dependency exists after symlinking OpenCode's `node_modules`, and falls back to `npm install --omit=dev` when it's missing.

2. **Bug 2 — Headless dispatch conflict with running server**: Added `_detect_opencode_server()` helper that checks `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` + port liveness (via curl health check then lsof fallback). Both `_build_run_cmd` and `_run_canary_test` now append `--attach <url> --password <password>` when a server is detected. Does NOT rely on `OPENCODE_PID` (intentionally excluded from worker envs per GH#6668).

3. **Workflow improvement — Triage failure visibility**: When the triage review output is suppressed by the safety filter (infra markers, missing `## Review:` header, or empty output), a `triage-failed` label is now added to the issue. This makes failed triage visible on the issue timeline instead of only appearing in pulse logs. The label is automatically removed when a successful triage review is posted.

## Files Changed

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json` — added `dependencies.@bufbuild/protobuf`
- `EDIT: setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` — verify critical dep after symlink, npm install fallback
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — `_detect_opencode_server()`, patched `_build_run_cmd` and `_run_canary_test`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `triage-failed` label on suppressed triage output

## Runtime Testing

| Risk | Assessment |
|------|-----------|
| Level | High — headless dispatch infrastructure |
| Verification | `self-assessed` — no opencode serve environment available locally to runtime-test. ShellCheck clean. JSON valid. Logic verified against issue reproduction steps. |

## Key Decisions

- **Port detection strategy**: Check `OPENCODE_PORT` env (default 4096), verify via curl health check on `/api/session/list` (returns 401 without auth but proves server is up), fallback to `lsof` port check. More robust than hardcoding port 4096.
- **No OPENCODE_PID dependency**: The detection uses `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` + port liveness, not `OPENCODE_PID`. This works for both the pulse's own context (where PID is set) and isolated worker envs (where PID is stripped per GH#6668).
- **triage-failed label vs comment**: Label is preferable — it's filterable, visible in issue lists, and doesn't add noise to the timeline. Removed automatically on successful triage.

title: GH#17671: remove unauthorized external code, revert unreviewed PRs, harden merge gates
body:
## Summary

Security hotfix responding to unauthorized code merged via external contributor PRs that bypassed the cryptographic approval gate.

### Removals and reverts

- **Removes** `.github/workflows/hol-skill-validate.yml` — unauthorized `hashgraph-online/skill-publish` GitHub Action introduced by `internet-dot` via PR #17671. Ran third-party Node.js code and called out to `hol.org` on every push to main and every PR. Merged by `alex-solovyev`.
- **Reverts** PR #3846 (`OnlyTerp`): re-adds S1192 string literals exclusion to `sonar-project.properties`. Filed as #17869 for maintainer review.
- **Reverts** PR #17685 (`saschabuehrle`): restores original stat fallback chain and inline WAL pragma in `opencode-db-archive.sh`. Filed as #17870 for maintainer review.

### Gate hardening (prevents recurrence)

- **Fixes** `maintainer-gate.yml` — now checks the PR's own `needs-maintainer-review` label, not just linked issue labels. This closes the bypass vector where external PRs without linked issues passed the gate automatically.
- **Fixes** `review-bot-gate.yml` — disables rate-limit grace period and `skip-review-gate` label for `external-contributor` PRs. External code must always receive a real code review.
- **Fixes** `.coderabbit.yaml` — adds `external-contributor` as a positive label trigger so CodeRabbit prioritises external PRs even when rate-limited.

## Root Cause (GH#17671 post-mortem)

1. External contributors opened PRs adding/modifying code
2. `pr-triage-gate.yml` correctly applied `needs-maintainer-review` label to the PRs
3. `maintainer-gate.yml` checked for linked issues, found none, posted SUCCESS — **it never checked the PR's own labels**
4. Collaborators merged the PRs — the gate was green because it only looked at linked issue labels

## Verification

After merge:
- `hol-skill-validate.yml` no longer exists
- `sonar-project.properties` has e5 (S1192) suppression restored
- `opencode-db-archive.sh` has original stat fallback and inline WAL
- Open an external contributor PR without linked issues → maintainer-gate should BLOCK
- External contributor PR with rate-limited bots → review-bot-gate should NOT pass via grace

## Review issues created

- #17869 — Review reverted OnlyTerp PR (sonar config change)
- #17870 — Review reverted saschabuehrle PR (stat/WAL changes)

Resolves #17671

title: GH#17873: fix triage review dedup dead-letter state on suppressed reviews
body:
## Summary

Fixes the triage review dead-letter state where suppressed reviews permanently block retries via the content-hash dedup cache.

**Root cause**: `_triage_update_cache` was called unconditionally after every triage attempt (GH#17746). When the safety filter suppressed a review (e.g., missing `## Review:` header), the hash was still cached, causing all subsequent pulse cycles to skip the issue with "content unchanged since last triage".

**Observed on GH#17861**: Worker produced 151K chars of valid review but the output was suppressed because it lacked the exact `## Review:` header. Every subsequent pulse cycle hit the dedup cache.

## Changes

1. **Dedup cache: only write on successful post** — `_triage_update_cache` moved inside the `triage_posted == "true"` guard. Failed/suppressed attempts are retried on the next pulse cycle, allowing transient formatting issues to self-heal.

2. **Broaden review header matching** — Changed from exact `^## Review:` to `^## .*[Rr]eview` in both the sed extraction and jq comment filter. This accepts variant headers like `## Triage Review:`, `## Review Summary:`, `## Review` (no colon).

3. **Cleared stale cache** for GH#17861 so it gets retried on the next pulse cycle.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `_triage_content_hash()`, review extraction, cache logic in `dispatch_triage_reviews()`

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: Medium (pulse infrastructure, no user-facing impact)
- **Verification**: shellcheck clean on modified sections. Logic review: the only behavioral change is (a) suppressed reviews are retried instead of permanently cached, and (b) more header variants are accepted.
- **Status**: `self-assessed` — changes are to pulse dispatch infrastructure, not testable via unit test without a full pulse cycle.

Resolves #17873

title: hotfix: Bash 3.2 heredoc-in-subshell parse error crashing pulse dispatch
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `_create_requeue_issue()` used `$(cat <<HEREDOC ...)` which triggers a known Bash 3.2 bug — literal `)` inside a heredoc nested in `$()` is misinterpreted as closing the command substitution
- **Impact**: Every 2-minute pulse cycle crashed on parse at line 5754 before reaching dispatch — **zero workers dispatched** for open issues
- **Fix**: Replace `$(cat <<HEREDOC ... HEREDOC)` with `IFS= read -r -d '' var <<HEREDOC || true` to avoid the `$()` nesting entirely
- Also fixes `routine-schedule-helper.sh` `${day,,}` (Bash 4+ syntax) → `tr` for Bash 3.2 compat

### Reproduction

```bash
# This fails on macOS Bash 3.2:
/bin/bash -n <<'TEST'
f() {
  x=$(cat <<INNER
text with (parens) here
INNER
  )
}
TEST
# Error: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
```

### Verification

```bash
/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh  # must exit 0
/bin/bash -n .agents/scripts/routine-schedule-helper.sh  # must exit 0
```

title: t1933: fix(pulse): gate PID-based worker recovery on runner identity
body:
## Summary

In multi-runner setups, the stale assignment reset in `normalize_active_issue_assignments()` uses `pgrep` to check if a worker process is running. This only checks local processes — a worker dispatched by Runner B is invisible to Runner A's `pgrep`, causing false stale assignment resets that interrupt active workers on other machines.

## Root Cause

`pulse-wrapper.sh` Pass 2 (stale assignment reset, GH#16842) checks:
1. `pgrep -f "issue.*${stale_num}"` — local process check only
2. Worker log recency — local filesystem only

Neither check can detect workers running on other machines sharing the same GitHub login.

## Fix

Before resetting a stale assignment, extract the `Worker PID` from the dispatch comment. If the PID is absent locally but the dispatch comment is still within `WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME` (default 3h), assume the worker is running on another machine and skip the reset. Only reset cross-runner dispatches after `WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME` has elapsed.

This preserves the existing local-runner PID check (fast path) while adding a time-based expiry fallback for cross-machine dispatches.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `normalize_active_issue_assignments()` Pass 2 (lines ~3879-4002)

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **Medium** (polling loop modification, no runtime available) — `self-assessed`

- Bash syntax check: `bash -n .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` → exit 0
- Logic verified by code review: cross-runner guard only activates when dispatch PID is absent locally AND dispatch comment age < WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME
- Existing behavior preserved: local worker detection via pgrep unchanged; worker log recency check unchanged

Resolves #17889

title: t2030: add pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh (step 1/2)
body:
## Summary

Step 1 of the pulse prefetch refactor (t2030). Introduces a standalone helper that collapses per-repo `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` calls into one `gh search issues --owner X` / `gh search prs --owner X` per owner.

For the current pulse workload (42 pulse-enabled repos across 2 owners), this reduces the prefetch phase from ~84 `gh` calls per cycle to **4** — a ~20x reduction in GitHub API consumption, staying well within the 5000/hr GraphQL budget even at high pulse frequency.

## Why

Observed on 2026-04-07/08: GraphQL rate limit exhausted repeatedly during normal pulse operation, blocking worker dispatch. Stopgap: trimmed pulse-enabled repos from 42 to 6. This PR makes the structural fix so the 42 repos can be re-enabled.

## What this PR does

- Adds `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` (standalone, 507 lines, shellcheck clean)
- Commands: `refresh`, `cache-path --kind issues|prs --slug owner/repo`, `clear`, `status`
- Cache at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/batch-prefetch/` with per-owner TTL markers
- Per-slug output files mirror the shape of `gh issue list --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees` after `repository` field is stripped during split

## What this PR does NOT do

- `pulse-wrapper.sh` is untouched. Step 2 (follow-up PR) wires it to call `refresh` at the top of `prefetch_state` and check `cache-path` before each per-repo `gh` call, with fallback to the existing per-repo path on cache miss.
- No feature flag yet — the helper is inert until step 2 integrates it.

## Verification

Ran against live pulse-enabled repos:

\`\`\`
./.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh refresh
[pulse-batch-prefetch] Refreshing owner=superdav42 slugs=1
[pulse-batch-prefetch] Refreshing owner=Ultimate-Multisite slugs=5
[pulse-batch-prefetch] Refresh complete: owners=2 total_issues=27 total_prs=1
\`\`\`

- 6 repos, 2 owners, **4 gh calls total** (2 owners × {issues, prs})
- Shape verified: labels, assignees, number, title, updatedAt match existing consumer expectations
- `cache-path` returns path + exit 0 on hit, empty + exit 1 on miss or stale
- `clear` wipes cache; `status` shows counts and ages
- Shellcheck: zero violations

## Limitations

- `gh search prs` does not return `reviewDecision` or `statusCheckRollup`. Step 2 will leave the existing per-PR enrichment pass in place for those fields — only the bulk list is batched.
- Default search limit 1000/owner (raise via `PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_LIMIT`). At current scale the largest owner has ~20 open issues, so headroom is ample.

## Follow-up

Step 2 PR will:
1. Add `PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED` feature flag to `pulse-wrapper.sh`
2. Call `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh refresh` at top of `prefetch_state` stage
3. Modify `_prefetch_repo_issues` and `_prefetch_repo_prs` to consult `cache-path` before their existing per-repo `gh` calls

title: feat: crash-type-aware tier escalation, issue consolidation, and large-file simplification gate
body:
## Summary

Addresses systematic worker failure patterns observed across issues #17861, #17870, #17871, #17883 — where Sonnet-tier workers repeatedly crashed (30.4% failure rate, 182 orphaned worktrees) without producing commits on complex multi-file tasks, while simpler tasks in the same window succeeded.

### Changes

**A+C: Crash classification + immediate tier escalation**
- Workers now classified on failure as overwhelmed (read files, attempted work, could not complete), no_work (infra/setup failure), or partial (some commits, no PR)
- overwhelmed crashes trigger immediate tier escalation (threshold=1) — no more waiting for 2 failures when the model demonstrably struggled with task complexity
- Classification flows through all three detection paths: headless-runtime-helper, orphan cleanup, and worker-watchdog
- crash_type stored in fast-fail state JSON for diagnostics

**D: Issue consolidation gate**
- Pre-dispatch check: if an issue accumulates 2+ substantive comments (>500 chars, excluding dispatch/bot machinery) that modify scope, adds needs-consolidation label and defers dispatch
- Prevents implementing workers from wasting tokens reconstructing scope from comment archaeology

**E: Large-file simplification gate**
- Pre-dispatch check: if issue body references files >2000 lines, adds needs-simplification label and defers dispatch
- Integrates with existing simplification routine

**F: Graduated retry table**
- overwhelmed = escalate immediately (threshold=1)
- no_work / partial = default threshold (2 retries)
- Rate-limit failures = never escalate (provider capacity, not model capability)

### Files changed
- headless-runtime-helper.sh — crash type classification in _cmd_run_finish, pass-through in _report_failure_to_fast_fail
- pulse-wrapper.sh — orphan crash classification, consolidation gate, large-file gate, crash_type in fast-fail state
- worker-lifecycle-common.sh — crash-type-aware thresholds in escalate_issue_tier
- worker-watchdog.sh — crash type classification for watchdog kills

title: GH#17920: fix pulse throughput — reduce dedup TTL, clear dedup on crash, dispatch-first ordering
body:
## Summary

Fixes three bottlenecks causing 58% of pulse cycles to dispatch 0 workers despite 24 available slots and 40+ dispatchable issues.

**Observed metrics before fix:**
- 880 dedup blocks vs 622 dispatches (1.4:1 block ratio)
- 200 orphan cleanups (32% crash rate)
- 58% of cycles dispatch 0 workers
- `close_issues_with_merged_prs` stage takes ~262s per cycle
- `prefetch_state` takes ~128s per cycle
- Workers sit idle during ~7 min of housekeeping before dispatch

## Changes

### A. Reduce DISPATCH_COMMENT_MAX_AGE: 1800s → 600s
Workers either succeed in ~10 min or crash in ~2 min. The 30-min TTL wasted 28 min of dispatch capacity per crash. Aligned `STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` to match.

### B. Clear dedup on crash detection
1. **Added "Worker Watchdog Kill" to completion signals** — watchdog kill comments were NOT clearing the dedup guard, leaving killed issues locked until TTL expiry.
2. **Post "Worker failed" comment from orphan cleanup** — when a 0-commit worktree is cleaned up, immediately post a completion signal so the issue is dispatchable on the next cycle instead of waiting for TTL.

### C. Dispatch-first cycle ordering
Added early `apply_deterministic_fill_floor` call right after `calculate_max_workers` in `_run_preflight_stages()`, before heavy housekeeping stages. Workers cold-start in 25-30s and boot in parallel with cleanup. The main fill floor at cycle end still catches slots freed by housekeeping.

## Files Changed
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — TTL reduction, completion signal list
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — orphan crash comment, early fill floor
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — comment update (30-min → 10-min)

title: GH#17906: fix memory-pressure-monitor.sh review feedback (delimiter safety + here-string)
body:
## Summary

Addresses two code review findings from PR #17858 on `.agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh`.

### Fix 1: Here-string in `_matches_monitor_pattern` (line 457)

**Before:**
```bash
if echo "$full_cmd" | grep -iqE "$pattern"; then
```

**After:**
```bash
if grep -iqE "$pattern" <<<"$full_cmd"; then
```

Using `echo` to pipe variables to `grep` is problematic when the variable content starts with a hyphen (interpreted as a flag) or contains backslashes. The here-string form is safer and avoids spawning an extra subshell.

### Fix 2: SOH delimiter in `matched_rows` array (lines 546-582)

**Before:** `matched_rows+=("${pid}:${rss_mb}:${cmd_name}:${cmd}")` with `%%:*` / `#*:` parsing.

**After:** `matched_rows+=("${pid}"$'\1'"${rss_mb}"$'\1'"${cmd_name}"$'\1'"${cmd}")` with `IFS=$'\1' read -r r_pid r_rss r_cmd_name r_cmd <<<"$row"`.

Colon (`:`) is an unsafe delimiter because command names and arguments can contain colons (e.g., paths like `/usr/local/bin:something`, URLs, Python module paths). SOH (`\x01`) is a non-printable ASCII control character that never appears in process names or arguments.

### Fix 3: Numeric validation after parsing (lines 524-525)

Added `[[ "$r_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue` and `[[ "$r_rss" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue` after parsing each row. This provides defense-in-depth against injection attacks that could result from delimiter shifting caused by malicious data.

## Runtime Testing

**Risk level:** Low — monitoring script, no payment/auth/data-deletion paths.
**Verification:** `shellcheck .agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh` — zero violations.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh` — three targeted fixes at lines 457, 522-525, 547, 582

Resolves #17906

title: t1934: Broaden dispatch lock to all issues and PRs for prompt injection defense

## Summary

- Removes the NMR-only guard from `lock_issue_for_worker()` / `unlock_issue_after_worker()` so **all** dispatched issues are locked during worker execution — not just external contributor issues
- Adds **PR locking**: open PRs linked to the dispatched issue are locked/unlocked in tandem (workers read PR comments, same injection surface)
- Adds unlock to watchdog kill path (`worker-watchdog.sh`) and launch recovery path (`recover_failed_launch_state`)

## Why

Once a worker is dispatched, the issue state is frozen — any comment arriving after dispatch is either noise or adversarial. The previous NMR-only scope left internal issues and all PRs unprotected. This is defense-in-depth: even collaborator accounts can be compromised, and well-meaning mid-flight comments can derail workers.

## Changes

title: GH#17870: fix stat order to Linux-first across 6 scripts
body:
## Summary

On Linux, `stat -f` means filesystem status (not format string). So `stat -f '%z'` and `stat -f '%m'` output multi-line filesystem info to **stdout** before failing with exit code 1. When captured in `$()`, this corrupts variables used in arithmetic, causing hard exits under `set -Eeuo pipefail`.

The fix is to swap the fallback chain: `stat -c` (GNU/Linux) first, `stat -f` (BSD/macOS) second. On macOS, `stat -c` is an illegal option → stderr only (suppressed by `2>/dev/null`), no stdout pollution → falls through to `stat -f` cleanly.

This matches the existing correct pattern already used in `headless-runtime-helper.sh:262`.

## Files Changed

- `opencode-db-archive.sh`: `file_size_bytes()` and `get_active_worker_sessions()` — the primary bug causing DB archiving to never complete on Linux
- `opencode-sandbox-helper.sh`: `_latest_sandbox()` mtime check
- `pulse-wrapper.sh`: worktree `.git` mtime and worker log mtime (also added missing fallback)
- `mail-helper.sh`: 3× db size checks
- `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh`: 2× db size checks
- `site-crawler-helper.sh`: downloaded image size check (also added missing fallback)

## Testing

- ShellCheck: zero violations on all 6 modified files
- Pattern verified against `headless-runtime-helper.sh:262` (existing correct implementation)
- macOS: `stat -c` fails silently (stderr only), `stat -f` succeeds — correct result
- Linux: `stat -c` succeeds immediately — correct result, no stdout pollution

## Runtime Testing

Resolves #17870

title: t1936: add _gh_idempotent_comment() race-safe primitive for gate comments
body:
## Summary

- Adds `_gh_idempotent_comment()` — a shared, race-safe primitive that checks existing comments for a marker string before posting, and fails closed on API errors
- Migrates 3 gate comment callsites (consolidation, simplification, terminal blocker) from raw `gh issue comment` to the new function
- Eliminates duplicate gate comments caused by concurrent pulse instances racing on label-only TOCTOU guards

## Problem

Multiple pulse instances (different maintainers/machines) can race when posting gate comments. The label-only guard has a TOCTOU window: both pulses read "no label", both post, producing duplicate comments. Observed on GH#17898 where two identical "Issue Consolidation Needed" comments were posted 3 minutes apart by different maintainers.

## Solution

New shared function `_gh_idempotent_comment()` that:
1. Fetches existing comments via API
2. Checks for a marker string (e.g. `## Issue Consolidation Needed`)
3. Posts only if the marker is absent
4. Fails closed on API errors (never posts when it can't confirm absence)
5. Supports both issues and PRs via `entity_type` parameter

### Migrated callsites

| Gate | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| Issue consolidation | Raw `gh issue comment` | `_gh_idempotent_comment` |
| Large-file simplification | Raw `gh issue comment` | `_gh_idempotent_comment` |
| Terminal blocker | Inline grep on pre-fetched bodies | `_gh_idempotent_comment` (fresh API fetch) |

title: t1935: feat(pulse): deterministic blocked-by resolution via cached dependency graph
body:
## Summary

Implements a cached dependency graph for blocked-by resolution in the pulse, eliminating per-dispatch API calls and enabling automatic `status:blocked→status:available` relabeling every 2-min cycle.

## What

- **`build_dependency_graph_cache()`**: Builds a JSON cache of all blocked-by relationships across pulse repos once per cycle (5-min TTL). One bulk `gh issue list` per repo replaces N per-dispatch API calls.
- **`refresh_blocked_status_from_graph()`**: Reads the cache and relabels `status:blocked→status:available` for issues whose blockers are now closed. Zero API calls for resolution check; one API call per unblocked issue.
- **Enhanced `is_blocked_by_unresolved()`**: Reads from cache first (zero API calls), falls back to live API only when cache is absent or task not found in the task→issue map.
- **Main cycle hooks**: merge → build graph → refresh blocked → fill floor.
- **Constants**: `DEP_GRAPH_CACHE_FILE` and `DEP_GRAPH_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (default 300s).

## Why

Previously, `is_blocked_by_unresolved()` made 1-2 live `gh` API calls per dispatch candidate per cycle. With 50+ issues in the backlog, this adds significant latency and rate-limit pressure. More critically, `status:blocked` issues were only unblocked when the LLM supervisor ran (~1h delay), not every 2-min cycle.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — added 337 lines (2 new functions, enhanced existing function, 2 cycle hooks, 2 constants)

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level**: Medium (polling loop, state machine labels)
- **Verification**: self-assessed — logic is additive (cache miss falls back to existing live API path), no existing behavior removed
- **ShellCheck**: zero violations on new code (full-file check hits RSS limit on 13K-line file; new functions checked in isolation)

Resolves #17942
